meta.title: Hive: browser task → CLI worker → team
meta.subtitle: Local workbench path · terminal bytes carry interaction; authenticated team commands carry responsibilities and reports

components.label: Browser workbench
components.explanation: The traced normal desktop path is xterm onData → terminal client → run-specific WebSocket. IO carries input/output; control carries restore, resize and output acknowledgements. Both orchestrator and worker terminals use this transport. A separate user-input HTTP helper exists, but no browser call site was found in this checkout; it is not shown as the normal UI entry.

sources.label: Terminal output rendering and keyboard input

components.label: Terminal / CLI runtime
components.sublabel: PTY launch · stdin queue · WS fan-out
components.explanation: Overview grouping of AgentManager, the stdin dispatcher and the terminal stream hub, all inside Hive's Node.js runtime. AgentManager spawns the configured CLI under a PTY and writes its input. The dispatcher serializes formatted task/report injections and waits for post-start readiness. The hub forwards raw terminal input to the run and mirrors PTY output to connected browser viewers with snapshot restoration and flow control. This is not a remote worker queue service.

components.label: Orchestrator CLI process
components.explanation: An interactive CLI agent, not a deterministic scheduler in the browser. Hive instructs it to delegate a responsibility with team send by member name, continue independent work, and receive reports as incoming messages. The team helper POSTs to the local Hive API using workspace identity, agent identity and its token. Whether an arbitrary CLI follows these instructions or produces a correct final answer is not established by transport code.

sources.label: team send posts task and agent credentials

components.label: Worker CLI process
components.explanation: A separately spawned CLI attached to its own PTY and configured cwd. Startup supplies Hive endpoint/token context. Task-bound progress uses team message --to orchestrator --kind progress: it is stored but does not wake the orchestrator. team status explicitly wakes it without closing work. team report --dispatch <id> --seen <seq> sends the result and artifact references and ends that responsibility; it does not itself guarantee correctness or terminate a normal persistent CLI process.

sources.label: CLI cwd, token environment and launch

components.label: Team API + dispatch logic
components.sublabel: Agent token + role gate · durable state
components.explanation: Routes authenticate CLI identity/token and restrict commands by role. team send resolves a member, records a dispatch, then claims queued → submitted before injecting a formatted task. User-managed stopped workers stay queued until manually started; a never-started orchestrator-spawned worker may be started for its first dispatch. Startup readiness precedes replay. Status is logged and forwarded without closing work. A valid report atomically records the result, closes the submitted dispatch and queues report delivery. Report outbox draining injects into the orchestrator PTY; if it is down, the result remains queued for a later drain. HTTP 202 is acceptance, not proof of execution or delivery.

sources.label: Record, claim and inject after readiness
Status, atomic report and return delivery

components.label: Dispatch + message stores
components.explanation: Separate persistence responsibility, not another server. Runtime services share one SQLite connection for dispatch ledger, messages and report outbox. Production dataDir uses runtime.sqlite; callers without dataDir use an in-memory database. Reporting requires a submitted dispatch owned by the worker and the exact required seen sequence; a conflict rejects closure. Progress messages are recorded without an outbox entry, so they do not wake the recipient. A report becoming reported and its delivery to the orchestrator are distinct states.

cards.title: Task reaches a worker
items: Browser input reaches the orchestrator's PTY; the agent chooses when to run team send.
Claim queued → submitted, wait for startup readiness, then paste/submit the task.
A stopped user-managed worker stays queued until the user starts it; replay then delivers.

cards.title: Progress is not completion
items: PTY output is live terminal visibility for connected viewers, not a completion signal.
team message --kind progress records task history without waking the orchestrator.
team status wakes the orchestrator but leaves the dispatch open.

cards.title: Result returns to the team
items: team report closes only a submitted dispatch with the required seen sequence.
Result + report outbox commit together; delivery waits if the orchestrator is down.
Outbox → orchestrator PTY → CLI response → browser. Acceptance ≠ agent understanding.
